title: Chi-square Tests for Categorical Data
interviewAnswer: Chi-square tests compare observed categorical counts with counts expected under a null such as independence. They operate on counts, not percentages detached from sample size.
keyPoints: Expected cell counts matter for approximation quality.
why: Chi-square Tests for Categorical Data appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Expected cell counts matter for approximation quality.
deepDive: Chi-square tests compare observed categorical counts with counts expected under a null such as independence. They operate on counts, not percentages detached from sample size. Independence is a common null. Effect size still matters. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Test whether device type and conversion outcome are associated in a contingency table.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Chi-square Tests for Categorical Data make?
How would you validate or debug Chi-square Tests for Categorical Data in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
